Fit and pool mixture models across multiple imputations

Source: R/pool-imputations.R
pool_imputations.Rd

pool_imputations() estimates a mixture model from multiply imputed data and combines the results to account for uncertainty associated with missing values. It fits the same model specification to each completed data set, allowing parameter estimates to reflect the alternative plausible values supplied by the imputation procedure.

Class labels can differ across fitted mixture models even when their profiles are similar. Before pooling, the function matches individual profiles and group classes to those in the first imputation's fit. It then combines the aligned parameter estimates and covariance matrices using Rubin's rules. The resulting uncertainty incorporates both the estimated sampling variance within each analysis and variation in estimates between imputations.

The function returns pooled estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, and tests for eligible parameters, together with summaries of the individual analyses. Completed data sets must be supplied as a list or a mids object from mice; the function does not construct the imputation model.

Usage

pool_imputations(
  imputed,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  ...,
  level = 0.95,
  vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg"),
  adjust = .multilpa_p_adjust_methods
)

Arguments

imputed

The completed data sets: a list of at least two data frames with the same columns and rows in the same order, or a mids object from the mice package, which is completed here.

vars, id, n_profiles

As in multilpa().

...

Further arguments for multilpa(), such as n_group_classes, profile_covariates, group_covariates, categorical, n_starts and seed, used for every imputation.

level

Confidence level of the pooled intervals (default 0.95).

vcov_type

"observed" (default), "robust" or "opg", as in parameter_inference(), applied to every imputation's fit. For fits with sampling weights the default is "robust", and the other types are refused with latents_unsupported_weights; for fits with person centring or scaling the default is "robust" too, and the other types raise latents_unsupported_inference.

adjust

Multiplicity correction applied to the pooled p-values to give p_adjusted, as in parameter_inference(): "none" (default) or a method of stats::p.adjust(). The per-imputation tables are computed without correction.

Value

An object of class latents_pooled. as.data.frame() and get_results(x, "estimates") give one row per parameter, with the columns of parameter_inference() (level, outcome, term, parameter, estimate, standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low, conf_high) plus df (Rubin's degrees of freedom), within and between (the two variance components), riv (the relative increase in variance due to missingness) and fmi (the fraction of missing information). statistic and p_value are NA where parameter_inference() reports no test (variances and probabilities). get_results(x, "imputations") gives each imputation's aligned estimates, one row per imputation and parameter, and get_results(x, "fits") one row per imputation with its log likelihood, convergence and the label permutation that aligned it.

Details

Pooling is on the reported (natural) scale: the pooled estimate is the mean over imputations, and its variance is the mean within-imputation variance plus (1 + 1/m) times the between-imputation variance. Degrees of freedom follow Rubin (1987) with a large complete-data sample. Pooled intervals are symmetric t intervals, rather than the transformed Wald intervals used for bounded parameters by parameter_inference(). A structural constant, such as the probability of one for a single class, has zero within- and between-imputation variance and zero missing information. When the within-imputation variance is zero and the between-imputation variance is positive, riv is infinite and fmi is one.

Interpretation

Pooling requires an imputation model appropriate for the analysis and missingness assumptions, including the grouping structure where relevant. The number of classes and other model specifications remain fixed across imputations. Label matching resolves differences in numbering but cannot establish that substantially different class solutions represent the same underlying profiles.

Estimates are pooled on their reported scale. Consequently, symmetric confidence intervals for probabilities or variances can extend beyond their permissible ranges.

Choosing the imputation model

Valid pooling requires an imputation model compatible with the analysis model and the assumed missingness mechanism. Associations between covariates and indicators may be nonlinear because they depend on latent class membership. The imputation model should represent these associations, account for clustering, include relevant indicators and predictors of missingness, and propagate uncertainty in its estimated parameters. Imputing separately within modally assigned classes omits classification uncertainty. Complete-case analysis can also change the within-class indicator distributions when missingness depends on the indicators.

Conditions

latents_bad_data when imputed is not a list of at least two data frames with identical columns and row counts; latents_pooling_failed when any imputation's fit or inference fails (the message names the imputation and gives the original reason); latents_missing_package for a mids object without mice installed. Warnings from the individual fits are passed on as they are raised.

References

Rubin, D. B. (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley.

Meng, X.-L. (1994). Multiple-imputation inferences with uncongenial sources of input. Statistical Science, 9(4), 538–558.

van Buuren, S. (2018). Flexible Imputation of Missing Data (2nd ed.), section 5.2. Chapman & Hall/CRC.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# Illustrative completed data sets for demonstrating the pooling interface.
# For an analysis, supply data generated by an appropriate imputation model.
completed <- lapply(seq_len(2), function(i) {
  within(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),
         previous_grade <- previous_grade + rnorm(length(previous_grade), sd = 0.1))
})
pooled <- pool_imputations(completed, c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"),
                           "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1,
                           profile_covariates = "previous_grade",
                           n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
pooled
